sections.h2: Listing or fast sale in Gurnee
sections.html:
Most owners weigh the condition of the house against the days they can afford to wait. A move-in-ready home can justify a listing, while a house that needs work or an owner facing a deadline points toward an as-is purchase. All three routes end the same way, with a deed recorded at the Lake County Clerk.

  • Agent listing: a wider pool of buyers, balanced against inspections, repair requests and a lender's timetable.
  • Owner-handled sale: you keep the commission and take on showings, disclosures and the contract.
  • As-is cash sale: a shorter path to closing, with the buyer assuming whatever repairs remain.

Gather recent sales on your street first, because Gurnee houses are priced against their neighbors, not against the resort attractions nearby.

Gurnee sits on the Des Plaines River in Lake County, roughly 40 miles north of Chicago and 50 miles south of Milwaukee, next to Waukegan. Interstate 94 splits the village into an older east side and a newer west side. Pace buses link Gurnee with Waukegan and Grayslake, and a CPKC rail line between Chicago and Minneapolis runs through town.

Six Flags Great America, Gurnee Mills and the Great Wolf Lodge resort bring millions of visits a year. Buyers will want to know how close a house sits to the I-94 corridor and the attraction areas, so be ready to describe its location.

Gurnee closings move fastest when the paperwork starts before the contract is signed. A workable order looks like this.

  1. Pull your permit records and any elevation certificate or flood information, since buyers near the Des Plaines River will ask.
  2. Confirm which elementary district your address falls in, and write it into the listing.
  3. Check with the Building Division about any open permit or recent window, furnace, water heater or roof work, and keep the contractor's paperwork.
  4. Choose your route: listing, owner-handled sale or as-is cash offer. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and usually the repair requests that follow it.
  5. Ask your title company to line up the notary, the legal description, the PTAX-203 and the tax bill address for the deed.
  6. Use the Village's Start, Stop or Make Changes page to end your water service near the closing date.

None of these steps needs a trip to Village Hall, and most can be done online or by phone. An owner who tackles them in order can usually give a buyer a firm closing date.

If the house has had work done without a permit, say so early. A buyer who takes the house as-is can accept the open items, but the contract should state clearly who is responsible, and the Building Division can tell you what it would require to close the permit.

Population is 30,458, with 11,900 households. In the 2020 census, 12,386 housing units were counted and 3.9 percent stood empty.

Gurnee draws a mix of buyers: families who want the school districts, commuters who want I-94 and the rail line, and people who like living near the shopping and entertainment area. Gurnee Mills has been open since 1991 and Six Flags Great America since 1976, so the attractions are long-established and part of the area's identity. The Warren-Newport Public Library, with more than 270,000 books, is another amenity families mention. Describe the house against that backdrop, and be straight about traffic or noise if the address sits close to the busy corridor.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Two elementary districts share the village. Gurnee School District 56 covers most of the east half through Spaulding (pre-K to grade 2), Prairie Trail (grades 3 to 5), Viking Middle School (grades 6 to 8) and River Trail (kindergarten to grade 8).

  • Woodland District 50 covers the west side and part of the east, with Primary, Elementary, Intermediate and Middle schools.
  • Warren Township High School, District 121, serves everyone: freshmen and sophomores at the O'Plaine Road campus, juniors and seniors at Almond Road.
  • Prairie Crossing Charter School takes kindergarten through grade 8 students from Districts 50 and 79.

Look up which side of town your address falls on before you describe the house.

sections.h2: Flood history and questions from buyers
sections.html:
The May 2004 storm brought the worst flooding in a century, closed schools and damaged dozens of homes and businesses. The Village names the low ground along the Des Plaines River and its tributaries as the most dangerous flood hazard area.

  • Look up your address on the Federal Insurance Rate Map and on the Village's inundation map.
  • Basements built more recently must have a sump pump ejection system, and the Village urges backups.
  • The Engineering Division, at 847-599-7550, keeps elevation certificates supplied by owners and historical flood records.
  • The Village's participation in the Community Rating System earns policyholders a 5 to 20 percent insurance discount.

A voluntary floodplain buyout program is also listed among the Village's flooding resources, along with a mailing list for flood updates.

Most construction, remodeling and improvement projects need a permit before work starts, and permits can help prevent issues in later property sales. Fences, reroofs, siding, water heaters, furnaces, driveways and window replacements go through an online One Stop portal. Larger projects such as additions and garages use a separate application. For inspections, call the Building Division at 847-599-7550 with 24 hours' notice and your permit number.

The Village sets a maximum U-factor of 0.28 for replacement windows in residential projects, so keep the contractor's paperwork if you replaced yours. Water arrives from Lake Michigan through the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency. The Village website has a Start, Stop or Make Changes page for your service, which is the place to end your account near the closing date.

sections.h2: How a Gurnee deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Lake County Clerk's recording division in Waukegan takes the deed. The grantor's signature must be notarized and the page must show the buyer's address, a full legal description, the preparer, a return address and where tax bills go. A PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement is also required.

Six municipalities require a local stamp before recording: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Gurnee is not one of them, but a quick call to the Village before closing settles it.

Your title company or attorney normally prepares and delivers the package. Ask them to confirm the notary, the legal description and the tax bill address a few days ahead, since a missing item at the recording counter pushes the date back.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Gurnee?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's recording division, in Waukegan. A notarized grantor signature, legal description and PTAX-203 or exemption statement are part of what it requires.

faqs.q: Does Gurnee have a local transfer stamp?
faqs.a: Six Lake County municipalities need one, and Gurnee is not among them. A quick call to the Village confirms it for your closing.

faqs.q: Where can I check flood history for a Gurnee house?
faqs.a: Start with the Village's Engineering Division at 847-599-7550. It keeps flood maps, elevation certificates provided by owners and historical flood records.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Gurnee house in?
faqs.a: East side addresses mostly fall in District 56 and west side addresses in District 50, with all feeding Warren Township High School. Check your exact address.

faqs.q: What if my Gurnee house has work done without a permit?
faqs.a: Ask the Building Division about your permit record. Permits can help prevent issues in future sales, and an as-is buyer can take the house regardless.
